subject: Write a cleared store back, say when saving is paused, and let a download start before its URL goes (#67)
body:
A review of src/ui/App.tsx: a storage clear in another tab was treated as
a conflict, blocking saves and advising a reload with nothing to reload;
the session is written back instead. A refused command under a blocked
save now says so. The export anchor is attached and its URL revoked after
the download has started. An over-sized import names its real reason.
Escape inside a field leaves the field; Alt with a station digit is left
to the browser. Autoplay steps no longer write the ledger every 850 ms,
and the collection filter is built only while its panel is shown and its
inputs change. One deck size and one page size.

subject: Keep a hand scroll from opening the inspector, a mouse drag from cancelling, and controls quiet under autoplay (#65)
body:
A review of src/ui/BattleTable.tsx: a touch that started on an unplayable
card and scrolled the hand still opened the inspector after half a second;
any real movement now cancels the long press. The browser's pointer-cancel
at the start of a native mouse drag wiped the lifted card; it now ends only
a touch lift. A hover preview stayed on screen after its card left the
table; it clears when the card is gone. Exhaust and Hero-ability buttons
are disabled under autoplay like the hand. The chosen target resets with
the window, only a targeted card stages a destination, the Declare button
counts what it will declare, and the opponent portrait uses the shared
guest lookup. Also records the 102bf17 publish with its save fixture.

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Name every practice lesson explicitly and read the lesson guidance from its cards (#64)
body:
A review of src/sim/practice.ts: the lesson boards and completion rules
name every lesson and refuse an unknown one at the type level and at run
time; the lesson list and the schema's lesson ids are checked against each
other on load; the guidance text and choice labels read the companion's
name, cost and body, the spell's damage and the protection's bonus from
the cards, and the protection choices name the companions from the board.
No rule, card, schema or save changed.

body:

shop was open reset the arrival clock each time; openDoors is the one way
the sign, automatic hours and dawn open the shop and resets the clock only
when the doors were shut. Nightfall no longer posts a notice to a shop that

keeper level overwrote the level receipt's label with the mission's, so the

subject: Keep a rival's pump off a Hero, drop phantom targets on permanents, and never overturn a decided duel (#59)
body:
A review of src/sim/battle.ts: a rival holding a pump treated a damage
ability aimed at its Hero as a threatened companion and cast the pump on
the Hero, an illegal target that threw after the keeper's ability was paid;
only a companion is threatened now. A permanent cast with a chosen target
carried it on the stack although its enter effect aims at the hearth, so
planners scored damage companions as removal; permanents carry no target
and only spells count as removal. The upkeep loop kept drawing and burning
after the duel was decided and the state check could turn a win into a
draw; the loop stops and a decided result is never rewritten. The rival no
longer acts on a duel a cleanup discard just ended. One answer path serves
casts, passes and queued triggers; a duplicate guard and three superseded
comments are gone. Matrices re-measured: keeper 52% / 53%, unchanged.

body:
A review of src/sim/game.ts: a finished duel loaded from a save written
before its settlement could never pay out, since every battle command
refused it and leaving discarded the rewards; settlement is one function,
settleDuel, that the battle commands and leave-duel both run. The autoplay
chain seated the next guest from the current deck without the 100-card
check; it stops with a notice when the deck is not legal. A duel naming an
unknown guest seated the default guest in silence; it is rejected. Selling
no longer writes zero-valued foil and Illuminated entries, the Illuminated
slot is derived from PACK_SLOTS, and the schema-1 migration tolerates a
save without products. Seeded pack outcomes and saves are unchanged.

subject: Send no more attackers at a Hero than its loyalty needs (#55)
body:
Steady and Hero-minded pilots aimed every plain attacker at an opposing
Hero when the attack was not lethal, and damage past a Hero's loyalty is
lost, so most of such an attack was wasted. attackDestinations now sends the
weakest single attacker that fells the Hero, or for those two styles the
weakest attackers that reach its loyalty together, and keeps the rest on
the hearth; the power total is computed once. The redraw threshold scales
with the hand (fewer than two resources or fewer than two spells), both
seats choose their resource drop through plannedResource, and plannedCast
keeps each candidate's target from its filter pass. Matrices re-measured:
keeper 52% round robin, 53% next-three.

subject: Spend a shield before a Mourning drain, heal once per Welcome watcher, and preview queued triggers (#53)
body:
A review of the queued-trigger window found four rule defects: a Mourning
drain ignored the shield (so the rival's shield against a lethal drain never
worked), Welcome healed once for all watchers (so Fellowship grew once where
it grew once per watcher), a Recordwork watcher was spent when its trigger
was queued rather than when it drew, and lifelink gains queued the keeper's
Fellowship trigger first regardless of who was active. Every hearth hit now
runs through one hurt function that spends the shield first; Welcome heals
per watcher; Recordwork is spent on resolution; lifelink queues the active
side first as Mourning does. The combat preview resolves the queued triggers
as if nobody responded, so a lethal drain shows as lethal. A waiting trigger
is no longer a drop target or target button, and the practice and autoplay
stacks label a trigger instead of showing its source as a spell.

Round robin and next-three re-measured: keeper 52% and 54%, unchanged. The
120-day economy run is recorded in the acceptance record.

rival's deck style. Round robin re-measured: keeper 52%, unchanged.

body:
The rival's turn now runs its scored casts and Hero activations again in a
second main phase after combat, puts away its costliest cards at cleanup
instead of the last drawn, and takes the same one free opening redraw the

subject: Pilot the keeper's autoplay with the rivals' scored planners (#44)
body:
* Record the a91acd9 publish, capture save fixtures by script, and update dependencies

Main (a91acd9) is published to gh-pages (871cd6e); the squash merge made the
committed change-ledger snapshot stale, so it is regenerated from main.
scripts/capture-save.ts plays a representative game through the public
commands and writes the published build's save fixture. Dependencies move
to the versions Dependabot proposed in #28, #34, #37, #38, #39 and #40, with
react-dom matched to react (React refuses mismatched versions); #33's
upload-artifact is no longer used by the Checks workflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Queue automatic triggers on the stack with a response window

Gather, Fellowship lifegain, Spellcraft, Welcome, Recordwork and Mourning
now wait on the stack like spells instead of applying the instant their
event happens. One event wakes one item per owner naming every source, so
a window costs one pass; the active player's items wait first so the
other side's resolve first; triggers cannot be countered; and when the
window closes a trigger applies once per source still on the table and
fades for the rest. Spellcraft waits above the spell that woke it.

Rivals yield after a resource that wakes a trigger, shield a lethal
Mourning drain and otherwise let triggers resolve; autoplay passes them.
Stack items gain optional `trigger` and `sources` fields, so older saves
and the published fixtures load unchanged. The stack panel names a
waiting trigger and keeps it out of counter targets; the soundscape cues
a trigger waking. The rules tests walk each window, a new test covers
fading and the counter refusal, and a Chromium scenario checks the panel.
battle-rules is completed; the release scope moves queued triggers from
deferred to delivered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Author action motion from the public battle events

src/ui/action-cues.ts derives short-lived cues from the events and the
table before and after a command: the paid resource settles, a trigger's
sources lift with a ring, attackers strike toward the opponent and
blockers parry, a hearth or Hero that took damage shakes and a healed
hearth brightens, a cast or response rises onto the stack, and the recap
enters with the outcome. src/ui/action-motion.css owns every sequence
under a reduced-motion guard; the cues read only public state, and a
clock tick or a fresh duel at the same table produces none. Nothing in
the simulation changed. Three unit tests cover the derivation and the
Gather-window scenario checks the wake cue.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-measure the balance matrix after the trigger window

Keeper 45% overall as before; the eleven draws become none because a
mutual Mourning drain now resolves one side at a time; no recipe or
personality moves beyond ten-seed noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pilot the keeper's autoplay with the rivals' scored planners

The rival decision functions (targets, held responses, cast scores, Hero
ability values, attack destinations) now take the acting side explicitly
and are exported as plannedCast, plannedHero and plannedDeclaration. The
rival's turn calls them for its seat as before; the keeper's autoplay
calls them for its own seat in the personality its recipe suggests, and
takes the free redraw on an opening hand with fewer than two or more
than five resources. Every decision still reads only the acting side's
hand and the public table.

Full 1,680-duel matrix: the keeper's autoplay rises from 45% to 51%
(defensive rivals 26% -> 33%, reactive 38% -> 48%, recursive 37% -> 45%,
evasive 33% -> 41%), no draws, no unfinished duel. Rekindled Fellowship
still wins 80% as a rival and the authored Ember recipes stay at 25-27%
for the keeper. docs/RELEASE_SCOPE.md records the delivered action
motion instead of deferring it.

In the next-three matrix its keeper opponents are An Answer in Practice,
Keep the Near Fields and Beacon to Beacon, so the 80% measures the weak
authored Ember recipes as much as the defensive rival; it wins 63% as
the keeper's own recipe.

subject: Toward 1.0: rival personalities, deeper combat, practice duels and release evidence (#41)
body:
* Stop the compact-battle board height failing on sub-pixel layout

The assertion wanted each .battle-board at least 40px tall and CI measured
39.649, so the run failed on a difference no player can see. It has now
failed three times on unrelated changes: Dependabot #12 (workflow YAML only)
and #14, and the main run after #25.

Rounds the measured height before comparing, which keeps the usable-strip
intent while tolerating sub-pixel layout. A genuine collapse still fails.

Also refreshes the committed development change feed from merged main history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the rival guestbook, duel key moments and four practice lessons

Record wins, losses, draws and concessions per guest with the latest
reward, learned recipe and up to five public exchanges. Teach resource
payment, counterspell responses, blocking and targeted protection with
replayable borrowed-card lessons that use the real battle commands and
never change ownership or rewards. Browser runs now write screenshots
to Playwright's per-test output; `npm run test:screenshots` refreshes
docs/screenshots on request (DH-016).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Give rivals six tactical personalities and deepen combat rules

Every guest now pilots their recipe with an aggressive, defensive,
reactive, recursive, evasive or Hero-minded personality that changes
casting priority, removal timing, held response mana, protection,
counter thresholds, attack risk, blocks, gang blocks, Hero abilities
and attack destinations from the public table only. Combat gains
per-attacker destinations, any number of blockers per attacker with
attacker-ordered damage, Overrun spill through every blocker and
toggled block assignment; older saves load single blockers as lists.
The guest who lost the last meeting opens the next duel.

Add scripts/performance.ts (browser-emulated delivery report), widen
scripts/balance.ts to a 1,680-duel matrix from both seats with the
in-game autoplay in the keeper's seat, propose the 1.0 scope in
docs/RELEASE_SCOPE.md, run the browser suite under Playwright's
Firefox with PW_BROWSER=firefox, and assert that phone panel headings
never meet the close button (DH-017).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let guests speak in the guestbook and check a delivery budget

Each of the twenty guests carries four original rivalry lines chosen
by the saved record, and the guestbook names their tactical
personality with counterplay guidance for the keeper. The duel
welcome keeps the opening-seat note. scripts/performance.ts gains a
proposed delivery budget and a --check mode that fails on breaches;
the production build currently meets it. Browser tests skip
Chromium-only automation and WebGL scenes under Firefox instead of
failing, tolerate sub-pixel 44px controls and fall back when Firefox
rejects image decode().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add borrowed-recipe practice duels and style-aware autoplay

The card table offers a free practice duel: borrow any of the 28
recipes against any guest with no reward, record, recipe unlock or
clock; older saves default the new battle flag to false. Autoplay now
pilots the keeper's recipe in the style its own cards suggest, the
performance report pages through the whole binder, and
docs/RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md gathers dated evidence per scope area. The
balance matrix rerun shows the recipe spread survives the pilot
change, naming recall density versus Quickstep pressure as the first
tuning target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Extract the rival block planner as planBlocks over the public table
and let the keeper's autoplay use it, in the style the keeper's own
recipe suggests, instead of chump-blocking every attacker. Measure the
matrix again (keeper 46%, recursion recipes 73% and about 80% as
rivals, fast Ember 13–27%), record a reverted body-shape experiment
and a recipe-level tuning proposal for the owner, and let the balance
script run subsets with BALANCE_RECIPES, BALANCE_SEEDS and BALANCE_OUT.

* Check the change ledger against its own head commit

The pull-request Checks run tests GitHub's merge ref, whose first parent is
main, so the branch snapshot's newest commit was missing from the

* Trim the testing method: tiers, smoke tag, review-only screenshots and cases

docs/development/TESTING.md states what runs when: `npm run check` and
the covering spec files while developing, `npm run test:smoke` (six
@smoke Chromium scenarios, ~30 s) before a commit, the ordinary
`npm run test:gameplay` once before a publish, and the review run,

agreed checkpoint. Ordinary runs take no documentation screenshots
(`docScreenshot` is a no-op outside UPDATE_DOC_SCREENSHOTS=1) and run
one representative of each equivalent case through `reviewCases`, so
the suite is 55 scenarios in 2.1 min at two workers; the review run
keeps all 64. CI runs the checks tier and the Pages build only.

subject: Sweep the whole catalogue through the TypeSafe gate (#25)
body:
Scopes the questions so they can judge every set honestly, then records a
judgment for all 1,040 cards.

The boundary questions (Ashfall cause, Failing cause, disputed questions
settled as fact, graphic harm) apply catalogue-wide. A stone answering again
only applies from The Long Ash onward, because before RR 2311 that is canon.
Paintability, mechanic fit, framing and name confusability apply to authored
sets only: the older sets repeat one set tagline as every card's flavor, keep
their scenes in the briefs, and are named procedurally with deliberate
instant/sorcery twins, so judging them there reported the design, not defects.

Adds a catalogue-wide question for Theandril's open questions being settled as
fact, and a test asserting no judged card carries a blocking flag.

No blocking flags across 1,040 cards.

subject: Add The Quiet, a thirteenth 80-card volume (#19)
body:
* Add The Quiet, a thirteenth 80-card volume

Release 13 covers RR 2311–2313 from Book chapter VII: the stones fall
silent and every bargain becomes local. 80 Ember/Grove cards in three
strands (The Quiet Stones, The Near Fields, Beacon and Rider) use only
existing engine effects. Two ordinary-card recipes bridge to Rekindled
Hearths and The Long Ash, and older saves gain an empty Quiet shelf.

Card text passes a cached TypeSafe (jev-1.13.0) gate for lore boundaries,
paintability, framing and name confusion before any art is commissioned.
Each painting is one Codex built-in generation from its exact brief,
processed by the vendored factory and approved by exact hash after visual
review; five first generations were rejected and replaced. A review guard
checks that written findings report no defect before approval.

The helper page now reads catalog counts from a build-generated summary,
and structural tests use live set and card counts. Released baselines
stay pinned.
